explanation: The article ends its lead with the claim outright: the fall of the Bastille “was the flashpoint of the French Revolution”. The same lead is careful about what the fortress actually was — a prison holding seven inmates and already scheduled for demolition — and rests the claim on what it stood for rather than on what was taken: “at the time, the Bastille represented royal authority in the centre of Paris”. That is an argument about a symbol becoming an act, which is what `caused` says here, and it is the same shape this atlas already gives a war’s opening action: the Bohemian revolt and the Thirty Years’ War, the Moncada attack and the Cuban Revolution. It stays `probable`: an encyclopaedia lead reporting where the consensus sits is not a work arguing it, and rule 22 refuses `consensus` on a Wikipedia citation in any case. The storming is also filed as part of the revolution, and that is a separate statement — `parent` does not enter the adjacency, so the argument has to be made as an edge or not at all.
